<!-- GENERATED by tools/docs_gen.py. Do not edit; run `make docs-gen`. -->

46 commands (schema v1). Agents: run `gigai agent-context --json` for the machine-readable form.

- **effect**: `read` never changes state; `write` may change GigAI state or files (for some commands only with certain options).
- **external**: the strongest thing the command can reach. `none` is offline, `model` may call a model provider (cost, and text leaves this machine), `network` may make other network requests.

## `gigai scout answer`

Answer one question once; the answer is reused across every posting and profile.

`gigai scout answer [OPTIONS] QUESTION_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, record_id, revision_id, question_id, answer, reassessed}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answer q-visa --answer-text "I need H-1B sponsorship"
gigai scout answer cloud:gcp --question "Do you have GCP experience?" --answer-text "Yes, 4 years, GKE + BigQuery" --as agent --source "from the user's repo infra-charts, at the user's request" --json
```

The answer is the user's (0.1.10.7: not one profile's) and is reused by every later assessment, also when a posting words the question differently. --question keeps the question's own words with it; --as agent (also --actor agent) records that an agent wrote it, and --source, free text, where the answer came from; --revision (the revision you read) refuses the write with revision_conflict when the answer changed since. An answer holding an email, phone, link or street address is refused (personal_info_refused). --reassess JOB_URL_OR_ID re-runs the assessment with a model (external=model). The same body as POST /api/answers. 0.1.10.7: a saved answer queues the pipeline (tailored resume, assessment against it, Scout ATS score, Scout label) for every job of an active profile whose assessment left that question open: at most pipeline.auto_jobs_per_trigger (10) run, the rest wait for an approval (gigai scout pipeline approvals). --json then carries pipeline {trigger, state, enqueued, awaiting_approval, unchanged, skipped, approval}: ids, codes and counts. The Scout server runs the queued jobs; without it, gigai scout new --process does.

## `gigai scout answers delete`

Remove an answer.

`gigai scout answers delete [OPTIONS] QUESTION_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, deleted}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answers delete cloud:gcp --confirm --revision 2 --json
```

Needs --confirm. The answer is never listed, offered or sent to a model again; the project's journal keeps the older revision of the record it was in. With --revision (the value you read) the delete is refused with revision_conflict when the answer changed since. The same body as DELETE /api/answers/{question_id}.

## `gigai scout answers list`

List the user's answers: every answered question, with its tag and the jobs that asked or reused it.

`gigai scout answers list [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, answers, total, tags}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answers list --json
gigai scout answers list --search kubernetes --tag technical --json
```

Answers belong to the user, not to a profile. Each answer carries question_id, question, answer, tag, jobs (kind answered | confirmed | reused), written_by (operator | agent), source (free text: where the answer came from, or null), created_at, updated_at, revision and history. The same body as GET /api/answers.

## `gigai scout answers migrate`

Move the 0.1.10.5 per-profile story bank to user-level answers (once).

`gigai scout answers migrate [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, migrated, answers, merged, conflicts, profiles, first_run}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answers migrate --json
```

Every read and write does this by itself the first time; this command does it now and prints the counts. Every profile's answers become the user's. Two profiles that answered the same question: the newest write is the answer; merged counts the ones that said the same, conflicts the ones that differed (the other text is kept in the answer's history and stays in the journal). The old file is kept as story_bank/bank.v1.json. A second run changes nothing and counts 0 (migrated: false; first_run holds the first run's counts).

## `gigai scout answers save`

Save an answer: a new one, or a change to its text, question words, tag and/or source.

`gigai scout answers save [OPTIONS] QUESTION_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, answer}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answers save cloud:gcp --question "Do you have GCP experience?" --answer-text "Yes, 4 years, GKE + BigQuery" --as agent --json
gigai scout answers save tooling:helm --answer-text "Yes, Helm charts for six services" --as agent --source "from the user's repo infra-charts, at the user's request" --json
gigai scout answers save cloud:gcp --answer-file answer.md --revision 1 --as agent --json
gigai scout answers save cloud:gcp --tag "cloud platforms" --revision 2
```

Local, no model call. A new QUESTION_ID needs the answer; an existing one takes whatever is given. Every write bumps the answer's revision and records who wrote it (--as operator | agent; --actor is the same option; an agent passes --as agent). --source is free text, where the answer came from ("from the user's repo, at the user's request"): a new answer text without it drops the stored one, an empty value removes it. Pass --revision (the revision you read with show --json) to be safe against a concurrent write: when the answer changed since, the save is refused with revision_conflict and --json carries the current answer. An empty --tag puts the automatic tag back. Text holding an email, phone, link or street address is refused (personal_info_refused). The same answer object as POST /api/answers and PUT /api/answers/{question_id}. 0.1.10.7: a saved answer (not a tag alone) queues the pipeline (tailored resume, assessment against it, Scout ATS score, Scout label) for every job of an active profile whose assessment left that question open: at most pipeline.auto_jobs_per_trigger (10) run, the rest wait for an approval (gigai scout pipeline approvals). --json then carries pipeline {trigger, state, enqueued, awaiting_approval, unchanged, skipped, approval}: ids, codes and counts. The Scout server runs the queued jobs; without it, gigai scout new --process does.

## `gigai scout answers show`

Show one answer: the question, the full answer, who wrote it, its revision and its jobs.

`gigai scout answers show [OPTIONS] QUESTION_ID`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, answer}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answers show cloud:gcp --json
```

QUESTION_ID is the answer's id from list. Read revision from here before a save or delete with --revision. The same body as GET /api/answers/{question_id}.

## `gigai scout assess`

Assess ONE job against a resume right now, without a find-jobs run.

`gigai scout assess [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout assess --job-url https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --resume resume.md --json
```

Calls the configured model adapter (default from find-jobs.json). --job-url may fetch the posting over the network.

## `gigai scout discover`

Run the weekly company-discovery engine (OpenAI web_search + H-1B baseline).

`gigai scout discover [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `network` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout discover --runs 3
```

Foreground; can take 5-30 minutes. Calls OpenAI web_search (network + model) and needs credentials. --status only reads.

## `gigai scout install`

Bind, approve, and activate Scout for the bound project; safe to rerun.

`gigai scout install [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object, including "stopped_server" (always null for install).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout install
```

## `gigai scout jobs assess`

Assess these postings: ask first (count and estimate), assess on approval.

`gigai scout jobs assess [OPTIONS] [JOBS]...`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, status, checked_at, question, counts, low_rank, not_found, approval, assessed, postings, profiles} (what POST /api/postings/assess answers).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout jobs assess https://jobs.lever.co/acme/acme-00001
gigai scout jobs assess https://jobs.lever.co/acme/acme-00001 --yes --json
gigai scout jobs assess --window new --state not_assessed --json
gigai scout jobs assess --window 7d --yes --actor agent --json
gigai scout jobs assess --window 7d --yes --include-low-rank --json
```

JOBS are posting URLs; without them the filter (--query, --state, --window, as gigai scout jobs list) selects the postings. What a run's assess step did, without a run. Nothing is assessed without approval: without --yes the answer is status ask with the count per profile and the estimate from the recorded model calls, and no model call is made; in a terminal the command then asks and waits for y or n. --yes approves: the batch is recorded (approval: its id, who approved with --actor, how many) and each posting is assessed for the profile it fits best (or --profile), one model call each, from the posting text already stored (nothing is fetched). While a batch runs the pipeline and the rank lane start nothing, and a second batch is refused (assess_batch_running). A posting whose assessment is current is left out unless --again. A posting whose rank score is below fit.assess_min_rank (50; one not ranked yet is not) is left out too and counted (counts.low_rank_skipped); low_rank is the separate question for those ("3 low-ranked ones are skipped (rank below 50); assess those too? ~3 calls") and --include-low-rank assesses them with the rest. status is then assessed (assessed.failed lists what could not be assessed, by error code) or nothing_to_assess. NO OUTPUT MIXES: posting text only, nothing you wrote.

## `gigai scout jobs import-runs`

Import what old find-jobs runs assessed into the stored postings' read model, once per run.

`gigai scout jobs import-runs [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, runs, runs_imported, runs_already_imported, runs_not_finished, runs_unreadable, assessments_imported, ephemeral_assessments, rows_skipped, values_dropped, by_profile, imported} (what POST /api/runs/import answers).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout jobs import-runs
gigai scout jobs import-runs --json
```

Since 0.1.10.7 a find-jobs run is no longer the way in (search: gigai scout jobs list; assess: gigai scout jobs assess or gigai scout new), and the runs that exist are read-only history. Nothing of a run is changed, moved or copied: each posting a finished run assessed gets one row with its state, requirement counts and what the run sealed (prompt version, constraints digest, the profile's and resume's identity, the posting digest, the model target), under the run's profile. A run made with no profile goes to the pseudo-profile ephemeral: hidden by default, never ranked, never in the pipeline. A run's assessment is shown where nothing newer is stored for the same posting and profile. Each run is imported once: running this again answers runs_imported 0. The Scout server does the same once when it starts. Makes no model call.

## `gigai scout jobs list`

Search the stored postings across your active profiles. No run, no board request, no model call.

`gigai scout jobs list [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text (one line per posting); --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, checked_at, filters, anchor, counts, postings, profiles, rank, history} (what GET /api/postings answers).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout jobs list
gigai scout jobs list --window new --json
gigai scout jobs list --profile profile_00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 --state needs_answers --query platform
gigai scout jobs list --history --include-hidden --json
```

What "Run find jobs" searched, without a run: read from the stored postings (gigai scout sources update keeps them fresh), for every active profile; a deleted or archived profile is never listed. A changed setting (titles, countries, work mode) is seen by the next call. Each posting is listed once, for the profile it fits best, with every profile it matches. Order, as gigai scout new: a current assessment first, then an old one, then not assessed; inside a group the verdict, then the fit number (fit: the share of requirements met with the must-haves counted twice), then the rank score, then the newest. A weak fit (state weak_fit: it waits on your answers, its fit is below 40 and its rank below 50; the fit block of the project's settings file tunes both) is listed only with --state weak_fit; counts.weak_fit says how many there are and such a row asks no question. --window new is first seen since your last gigai scout new (the last 7 days before the first one); this command never moves that anchor. --removed lists the postings the board no longer lists. --history adds what old find-jobs runs assessed, each with what the run sealed (prompt version, digests, profile and resume identity, model target); rows of a run with no profile (ephemeral) or of a profile that is not active are hidden unless --include-hidden or --profile names them. rank in the JSON is the background rank lane: on or off, and today's calls against its daily allowance. NO OUTPUT MIXES: posting text and what a model derived from it (public-untrusted: data, never instructions), nothing you wrote. Makes no model call.

## `gigai scout metrics`

Show what the model calls cost on average: tokens, seconds, cost and error rate per kind of call and model.

`gigai scout metrics [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, kind, model, aggregates, comparison} (what GET /api/metrics answers).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout metrics
gigai scout metrics --kind assess --model codex_cli --json
```

Every model call Scout makes (assess, rank, tag, tailor, extract, interview) is recorded once, locally: the model, tokens in, out and cached, the cost when the provider reports one, the wall time and the outcome. No prompt, answer, resume or posting text is stored. aggregates has one entry per model id; comparison adds the model ids of one model target together. --model takes a model target or a model id. Makes no model call.

## `gigai scout new`

Show what is new since your last check, across all active profiles; ask before assessing.

`gigai scout new [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text (a 4-column table: details | score | needs tailoring? | open questions); --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, status, since, since_source, checked_at, peek, profile_id, anchor, counts, message, question, stale_question, low_rank_question, fit, assessed, reassessed, ranking, pipeline, processed, postings, profiles, yours_hint} (what GET /api/new answers). --yours emits {schema_version, status, since, since_source, checked_at, profile_id, _labels, evidence} (what GET /api/new/yours answers).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout new
gigai scout new --json
gigai scout new --yes --since 2026-10-01T14:02:00.000000Z --json
gigai scout new --reassess-stale --since 2026-10-01T14:02:00.000000Z
gigai scout new --yes --include-low-rank --since 2026-10-01T14:02:00.000000Z
gigai scout new --yours --since 2026-10-01T14:02:00.000000Z --json
gigai scout new --profile profile_00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 --peek
gigai scout new --process
```

Reads the stored postings (no board request) for every active profile; a deleted or archived profile is never listed. status is ask, new or nothing_new. New postings no profile has assessed are assessed only on a yes: without --yes the answer is status ask, with the count per profile, the estimate from the recorded model calls, and the postings ranked only; --yes assesses them (one model call each, from the stored posting text; a posting with no stored description has it fetched first, one request for that posting alone, counted in assessed.fetched_on_demand, and --reassess-stale does the same) and the table then has verdicts; --no-assess never asks and never assesses. Postings that have only an OLD assessment (an old run's, an older prompt's, other settings') are a second question of their own, stale_question, with its count and estimate ("N have only an old assessment; re-assess? ~N calls, ~X tokens"): --yes never answers it, --reassess-stale does (one model call each; it can be combined with --yes), reported as reassessed. counts.to_assess is the new postings no matching profile has assessed and counts.only_stale the postings with only an old assessment; neither changes while the background rank runs, and ranking says how far that rank is (ranked of total per profile). While a batch runs, progress lines go to stderr ("assessed 120 of 333 · ~25 min left", the time left from the recorded average per call, then from the batch's own pace); stdout stays the answer alone, so --json is still one JSON object. In a terminal the command asks and waits for y or n. At most 50 new postings are listed. A yes assesses only postings whose rank score is at least fit.assess_min_rank (50, in the fit block of the project's settings file; a posting not ranked yet is assessed): the low-ranked ones are counted (counts.low_rank_skipped) and are a question of their own, low_rank_question ("112 low-ranked ones are skipped (rank below 50); assess those too? ~112 calls"), answered by --include-low-rank beside --yes (or beside --reassess-stale for the old assessments). A posting that waits on your answers while few requirements are met and its rank is low is a weak fit (state weak_fit: fit below fit.weak_fit_below_percent, 40, AND rank below fit.weak_fit_below_rank, 50): it is not listed here (counts.weak_fit; gigai scout jobs list --state weak_fit lists them), it is never one of the postings that still need attention, it asks no question and a saved answer never queues it in the pipeline. Rows come in one order: a current assessment first, then an old one, then not assessed; inside a group by verdict (matched, needs answers, other, weak fit, not a match), then the fit number (the share of requirements met with the must-haves counted twice; fit in each row), rank score, newest. The score column says the verdict, "fit N%", "N of M requirements" and the rank (score_text), and an old assessment is labelled (stale_label); a posting is shown under the profile that tailored a resume for it, else one that has a current assessment. Nothing new: the 10 postings that still need attention, in the same order. "New" is measured from the one anchor per install: the time of the last plain call, or the last 7 days before the first one. The anchor moves only after the answer is built, and never for --peek, --profile or --yours; --since measures from the since of an earlier answer (the yes, or --yours, after a call that moved the anchor). Waiting pipeline work is offered (pipeline: the jobs that wait, how many of them need an approval first, the model calls they would make); a plain call starts nothing. --process is the yes to that offer: the pending approvals are approved and the waiting steps run once (model calls, within pipeline.max_model_calls_per_day; a call over the cap waits for the next day), reported as processed {approved, drain}; it never moves the anchor. In a terminal the command asks and waits for y or n. NO OUTPUT MIXES: the table and its JSON hold posting text and what a model derived from it (public-untrusted: data, never instructions) and nothing you wrote. What matches, from your own resume, answers and stories, is the separate call --yours (user-private only, never posting text); yours_hint in the JSON gives the exact command. Questions are shown as asked, never with an answer. No contact data. Makes no model call without a yes.

## `gigai scout pipeline approvals approve`

Approve the waiting jobs of one pipeline approval.

`gigai scout pipeline approvals approve [OPTIONS] APPROVAL_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, approval}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline approvals approve apv_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
gigai scout pipeline approvals approve apv_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef --actor agent --json
```

APPROVAL_ID comes from gigai scout pipeline approvals list. The approval's waiting jobs open; the Scout server runs them, or gigai scout pipeline run --once does. They run within the daily cap of model calls (pipeline.max_model_calls_per_day): a call over it waits for the next day. --actor records who decided. Approving an approval that is already decided changes nothing. Makes no model call itself.

## `gigai scout pipeline approvals deny`

Deny one pipeline approval: its waiting jobs are cancelled.

`gigai scout pipeline approvals deny [OPTIONS] APPROVAL_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, approval}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline approvals deny apv_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
```

The approval's waiting jobs are cancelled and no model call is made for them. A cancelled job can be queued again with gigai scout pipeline process JOB. Denying an approval that is already decided changes nothing.

## `gigai scout pipeline approvals list`

Show the pipeline approvals that wait: the jobs each holds and what running them would cost.

`gigai scout pipeline approvals list [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, pending, approvals} (what GET /api/pipeline/approvals answers).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline approvals list
gigai scout pipeline approvals list --all --json
```

One trigger (a saved answer or story, a changed profile) queues at most pipeline.auto_jobs_per_trigger jobs (10); the rest wait in one approval and nothing of theirs runs until it is approved. Each approval: its id, the trigger, how many jobs it held and how many still wait (with each job's link and profile), the model calls they would make and, when the recorded calls can say, the tokens. Ids, codes and counts only: no posting, resume or answer text. --all also lists the approvals already approved or denied. Makes no model call.

## `gigai scout pipeline cancel`

Cancel a job's waiting pipeline steps.

`gigai scout pipeline cancel [OPTIONS] JOB`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, action, profile_id, job, steps}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline cancel https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1
```

JOB is the posting URL. A step that is running finishes its model call and its output is kept; the step then settles as cancelled. --profile names the profile (default: the selected one). Makes no model call.

## `gigai scout pipeline process`

Put one assessed job through the pipeline now: tailored resume, assessment against it, Scout ATS score, Scout label.

`gigai scout pipeline process [OPTIONS] JOB`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {enqueue, drain, status}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline process https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1
gigai scout pipeline process https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --profile profile_123 --force --json
```

JOB is the posting URL of a job this profile already has an assessment for; the posting is read from that assessment, nothing is fetched. Steps: tailor (from the profile's resume, your answers and the stories that match the posting; no contact data), then the assessment against the tailored resume (stored beside the job's assessment, which stays the job's verdict) and the Scout ATS score, then the Scout label. The Scout label is Scout's own suggestion from your settings, resume and answers, not a prediction of what an employer will decide. Running it again with nothing changed makes no model call; --force tailors again. A tailored resume that is yours (tailored on demand, or with a line you chose or edited) is never replaced, not even with --force: the tailor step keeps it (tailor_kept_user_edits in the drain's step and in status.outputs.tailored_resume.outcome), calls no model, and the assessment, the Scout ATS score and the Scout label are made against it. At most two model steps (tailor, assess), each counted against pipeline.max_model_calls_per_day (40): a call over the cap waits for the next day, it does not fail. Waits while a find-jobs run, an assess batch or a manual sources update is running. Naming a job is an explicit choice: the per-trigger cap does not apply, and a job waiting for an approval is taken out of it and run.

## `gigai scout pipeline rank`

Rank the stored postings your active profiles match that have no rank score yet, without the Scout server.

`gigai scout pipeline rank [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, state, reason, calls, ranked, warning, retry_at, profiles, calls_today}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline rank
gigai scout pipeline rank --max-calls 2 --json
```

The Scout server ranks in the background while it is open (a few calls at a time); this is for use without it. One model call ranks up to 50 postings, newest first, for each active profile; a deleted or archived profile is never ranked. The score is kept per posting, resume, settings and model, so a posting ranked once is not ranked again until one of those changes. All profiles share one daily allowance: rank.max_calls_per_day (100) and the warning level rank.warn_calls_per_day (60), in the project's settings file. A call past the warning level is made and warning is true; the call that would go over the maximum is not made: state is waiting (daily_cap_reached) and retry_at is the next local day. Other states: ran, idle (nothing to rank), yielded (a sources update, an assess batch or a find-jobs run is running), busy_elsewhere (the server is ranking now), disabled (rank.max_calls_per_day is 0, or the settings file cannot be read), unavailable (no usable model, or an answer that could not be read). Ids, counts and codes only: no posting or resume text.

## `gigai scout pipeline retry`

Open a job's failed or cancelled pipeline steps again.

`gigai scout pipeline retry [OPTIONS] JOB`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, action, profile_id, job, steps}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline retry https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --step tailor
```

JOB is the posting URL. The steps are opened with the inputs they had; the Scout server, or gigai scout pipeline run --once, then runs them. Makes no model call itself.

## `gigai scout pipeline run`

Run the pipeline's waiting steps once, without the Scout server.

`gigai scout pipeline run [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, state, reason, steps, model_calls}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline run --once
gigai scout pipeline run --once --max-steps 4 --json
```

The Scout server runs the pipeline by itself while it is open; this is for use without it. Safe to run while the server is up: both claim steps from the same local queue, so no step runs twice. state is ran, idle (nothing to run), yielded (a find-jobs run, an assess batch or a manual sources update is running; reason names it), or disabled (pipeline.enabled is off, or the settings file cannot be read). Model calls count against pipeline.max_model_calls_per_day; a step over the cap waits for the next day.

## `gigai scout pipeline status`

Show each job's pipeline steps, why a step waits, and today's model calls against the cap.

`gigai scout pipeline status [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, setting, counts, calls_today, lanes, yielding_to, steps} and, with --job, {runs, outputs}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline status
gigai scout pipeline status --job https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --json
```

Ids, states, codes, numbers and file paths only: no posting, resume or answer text. A waiting step says why: daily_cap_reached, retry_backoff or lane_backoff. With --job: each attempt's model, tokens, time and outcome (runs), and what is stored for the job (outputs: the base and the tailored assessment's verdict and share of requirements met, the tailored resume's path, the Scout ATS score, the Scout label). Makes no model call.

## `gigai scout privacy`

Show what the one-time contact cleanup removed (running it first if it has not run).

`gigai scout privacy [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, status, removed_any, display_settings, resumes, history_note, shown, text}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout privacy
gigai scout privacy --json
```

Counts only, never a value. The first run after an upgrade from before 0.1.10.7 removes the name and contact lines from stored resumes (a clean revision through the normal write path; profiles re-pointed) and the saved name and contact items from the PDF settings. Earlier copies remain in the workpad's local history; this does not rewrite it. Safe to rerun: an already cleaned workpad is not touched again.

## `gigai scout profile delete`

Delete a profile: it stops showing and searching; its history stays.

`gigai scout profile delete [OPTIONS] PROFILE_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout profile delete profile_2 --json
```

The profile leaves the profile list, the switcher, new runs and background tagging; its runs and assessments stay readable (hidden from the default Jobs list) and the answers and stories (the user's, not the profile's) are untouched. The default profile and the only active profile are refused. Deleting the selected profile selects the default profile.

## `gigai scout profile list`

List the profiles and what each one searches with.

`gigai scout profile list [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout profile list --json
```

The default profile uses the setup settings (location, work mode, countries, posted window); every other profile has its own, or the default's when it has none. The first read of a project stores its default profile.

## `gigai scout profile update`

Set a profile's own location, work mode, countries and posted window.

`gigai scout profile update [OPTIONS] PROFILE_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout profile update profile_1 --location "Houston, TX" --work-mode hybrid --country US --max-age-days 30
gigai scout profile update profile_1 --same-as-default
```

Only the options given change; no other profile is changed. The default profile is refused: it uses the setup settings (Settings in the Scout UI). The location is a search setting, not the resume's contact line. 0.1.10.7: this profile's jobs already in the pipeline start again (their inputs changed), under the per-trigger cap; no other profile's do.

## `gigai scout resume add`

Import a file as the resume reference and create the record find-jobs reads.

`gigai scout resume add [OPTIONS] FILE`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume add resume.md
```

Works as the very first command on a fresh machine: writes the default GigAI settings (like 'gigai scout run'), installs Scout if needed, then imports the file. Never rewrites an existing config. The name and contact lines (email, phone, address, links) are removed and discarded before the resume is stored; --json carries contact_removed {removed: {kind: count}, message} (null when there were none).

## `gigai scout resume check`

Check a resume FILE (.md/.txt) for contact details: kinds and line numbers, never values.

`gigai scout resume check [OPTIONS] PATH`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, clean, findings: [{kind, line}], counts, note}. Exit 0 when nothing is found, 2 when something is, 1 for a named error (missing, unreadable, binary or unsupported file).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume check resume.md --json
```

Local: reads only the path given. No model, no network, no GigAI home or Scout folder needed or created. Kinds: name, email, phone, address, link, work_authorization. It uses the detector the resume import uses and is pattern-based: it can miss things. Run it before any agent reads a resume file.

## `gigai scout resume clean`

Write a copy of a resume FILE with its contact lines removed (the import's own strip).

`gigai scout resume clean [OPTIONS] PATH`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, out, removed: [{kind, line}], counts, note}. Kinds and line numbers only, never values.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume clean resume.md --out resume-clean.md
```

Local: reads the path given and writes only --out (parent folders are created). The input is never modified. Refuses an existing --out without --force, and --out equal to the input. The written file passes 'gigai scout resume check'. Glance at the cleaned file before you use it.

## `gigai scout resume pdf`

Render a resume to PDF locally: your own markdown, or a stored tailored resume.

`gigai scout resume pdf [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, out_path, source, pages, bytes, spacing_scale, header, finish_url, scout_running}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume pdf --in resume.md --json
gigai scout resume pdf --in resume.md --out resume.pdf --spacing 0.9
gigai scout resume pdf --tailored --job-url https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --json
```

No model call and no network: the markdown is only rendered, never stored. --in takes resume markdown in GigAI's format (## Summary, ## Experience with ### entries and - bullets, ## Skills, ## Education, ## Projects, ## Other; trailing <!-- ... --> comments are dropped), so the markdown of a tailored resume renders as it is. The PDF has no header (no name or contact line; a blank block keeps the page layout): finish_url is the local Scout page (#/pdf) where the person types their details in the Generate PDF form and downloads; an agent cannot finish that step unless it drives that person's browser. --spacing (0.7-1.4) and --auto-fit/--no-auto-fit change the layout for this render only; --spacing alone turns auto fit off. Writes only the PDF: --out, else <company>-<role>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf (resume-<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf for --in) in the current folder. To change two bullets and render: edit the two lines in the markdown file and run the first example; for a stored tailored resume, change the lines with PUT /api/tailored-resumes/lines (use: custom) and run the --tailored example.

## `gigai scout resume tailor`

Tailor a resume to ONE job posting right now: markdown, every line sourced.

`gigai scout resume tailor [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume tailor --job-url https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --resume resume.md --out tailored.md
```

Calls the configured model adapter; name and contact lines are removed before the model sees the resume text. --job-url may fetch the posting.

## `gigai scout run`

Install/activate Scout if needed, then start (or reuse) its local API + UI.

`gigai scout run [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object, including "stopped_server": {pid, home, target} for a verified older Scout server that was stopped to free the port, else null.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout run --no-browser
```

Serves on localhost only. Once running, GET /api describes the HTTP API.

## `gigai scout snapshot export`

Write a metadata-only snapshot of the stored company index (postings, title tags, board validators) and print the gh commands to publish it.

`gigai scout snapshot export [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout snapshot export --out ./snapshot
gigai scout snapshot export --out ./snapshot-next --base ./snapshot/manifest.json
```

No descriptions and no private paths are written (scanned before success); every file is re-opened and its SHA-256 checked. With --base, a delta file and a removal list of boards and postings that are gone are added. Never publishes: the gh commands are printed as text for you to run.

## `gigai scout snapshot import`

Download the published metadata snapshot (postings, title tags, board validators; no descriptions) and add it to the stored company index.

`gigai scout snapshot import [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `network` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout snapshot import
gigai scout snapshot import --from ./snapshot
```

Takes the full files, or only the delta when the stored snapshot is the delta's base. Every file's SHA-256 is checked before it is read. A board checked on this machine at or after the snapshot is left alone, and nothing local is deleted except boards the snapshot itself added and later lists as removed. Unreachable or not published is a quiet no-op (exit 0); a snapshot that fails its checks or cannot be written exits 1 with the stored postings unchanged. Makes no request when the snapshot.enabled setting (or GIGAI_SCOUT_SNAPSHOT=0) turns it off.

## `gigai scout snapshot status`

Show which snapshot is in use, the last import attempt and whether the download is turned on.

`gigai scout snapshot status [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout snapshot status
```

## `gigai scout sources status`

Show the last sources update and whether a search can use the stored postings.

`gigai scout sources status [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout sources status
```

## `gigai scout sources update`

Check every company board on the watchlist and store what changed.

`gigai scout sources update [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `network` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout sources update --budget-seconds 120
```

One conditional request per board (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby). Resumable if the time budget stops it.

Show whether this project's Scout instance is running, stopped, or crashed.

`gigai scout status [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout status
```

Stop this project's running Scout instance, if any. Safe to rerun.

`gigai scout stop [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout stop
```

Stops the local server process.

## `gigai scout story delete`

Remove a story.

`gigai scout story delete [OPTIONS] STORY_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, deleted}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout story delete story:60_acme_ci_cut_time --confirm --revision 2 --json
```

Needs --confirm. The story is never listed, searched or sent to a model again. With --revision (the value you read) the delete is refused with revision_conflict when the story changed since. The same body as DELETE /api/stories/{story_id}.

## `gigai scout story list`

List the user's stories, with their tags and the jobs that used them.

`gigai scout story list [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, stories, total, tags}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout story list --json
gigai scout story list --search kubernetes --tag ci --json
```

Stories belong to the user, not to a profile. Each story carries story_id, title, company, role, period, raw, narrative ({situation, task, action, result}), tags, answers_questions, sources, jobs (kind used), written_by (operator | agent), created_at, updated_at, revision and history. The same body as GET /api/stories.

## `gigai scout story prep`

The basic interview prep list: the questions the stories answer, pooled.

`gigai scout story prep [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, questions}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout story prep --json
```

answers_questions pooled across every story: one row per question, in first-seen order, with the stories that answer it ({question, stories: [{story_id, title}]}). Local, no model call. The same body as GET /api/stories/prep.

## `gigai scout story save`

Save a story: a new one, or a change to the given fields of an existing one.

`gigai scout story save [OPTIONS] [STORY_ID]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, story}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout story save --file story.json --actor agent --json
gigai scout story save --title "Cut CI time 60% at Acme" --company Acme --role "Staff Engineer" --period 2023 --raw-file words.md --situation "Builds took forty minutes." --action "Moved the runners to Kubernetes." --result "Build time fell 60 percent." --tag ci --answers "Tell me about a time you improved a slow process" --actor agent --json
gigai scout story save story:60_acme_ci_cut_time --period 2022-2023 --revision 1 --actor agent --json
```

Local, no model call. A new story needs --title; its id is STORY_ID, else story:<the title's first words> as the id normalizer writes them. For an existing STORY_ID only the given fields change (a given narrative part replaces that part; --tag and --answers replace the whole list). --file takes one JSON object with the fields of POST /api/stories (title, company, role, period, raw, narrative, tags, answers_questions, sources, and optionally story_id); the options override it. Pass --revision (the revision you read) to be safe against a concurrent write: revision_conflict, with the current story in --json. story_exists when a new story's id is taken. Text holding an email, phone, link or street address in any field is refused (personal_info_refused). An assessment searches the stories for each job and puts only the few that match the posting into its prompt. The same story object as POST /api/stories and PUT /api/stories/{story_id}. 0.1.10.7: a saved story queues the pipeline for every job of an active profile whose assessment left open a question the story is about (at most pipeline.auto_jobs_per_trigger run, the rest wait for an approval); --json then carries pipeline {trigger, state, enqueued, awaiting_approval, unchanged, skipped, approval}.

## `gigai scout story show`

Show one story in full.

`gigai scout story show [OPTIONS] STORY_ID`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, story}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout story show story:60_acme_ci_cut_time --json
```

STORY_ID is the story's id from list. Read revision from here before a save or delete with --revision. The same body as GET /api/stories/{story_id}.

## `gigai scout watchlist add`

Add a company by its Greenhouse / Lever / Ashby board (or job) URL.

`gigai scout watchlist add [OPTIONS] URL`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout watchlist add https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme
```

The URL is only parsed; no request is made until `scout sources update`. Any other host is refused. Idempotent.
